saints.name: Nativity
saints.title: The Nativity of Our Lord Jesus Christ (Lidat)
saints.notes: Christmas in the Ethiopian Orthodox Church, celebrated on Tahsas 29 (January 7 Gregorian).

saints.name: St. Frumentius
saints.title: Saint Frumentius (Abba Salama), Apostle to Ethiopia
saints.notes: Frumentius (c. 300–360 AD) was the first bishop of Axum and the Apostle of Ethiopia. A Syrian Christian from Tyre, he converted King Ezana and established Christianity in Ethiopia. He was consecrated by St. Athanasius of Alexandria.

saints.name: Abeluzius
saints.title: Abeluzius
saints.notes: Abeluzius is a saint of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. He is commemorated with a feast day of January 15. Little else is known of the person.

saints.name: Theodosius I
saints.title: Theodosius I
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Timket
saints.title: Feast of the Epiphany / Theophany (Timket)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Epiphany (Timket), the most spectacular Ethiopian feast. Celebrates the Baptism of Christ in the Jordan.

saints.name: St. Michael
saints.title: Monthly Feast of St. Michael the Archangel
saints.notes: St. Michael is commemorated on the 12th of every Ethiopian month. The Tir (January) feast is the principal annual commemoration.

saints.name: Abba Tsahma
saints.title: Abba Tsahma
saints.notes: Abba Tsahma or Sähma  (probably fl. late 400s and early 500s A.D.) was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. He was known as a scholar.

saints.name: St. Cyril of Alexandria
saints.title: Saint Cyril of Alexandria, Pillar of the Faith
saints.notes: St. Cyril of Alexandria (376–444) defended the title Theotokos (God-bearer) for the Virgin Mary at the Council of Ephesus (431). Venerated by the Ethiopian church as Pillar of the Faith.

saints.name: Martyrs of Debre Damo
saints.title: Holy Martyrs of Debre Damo Monastery
saints.notes: The monks of Debre Damo monastery who were martyred during the invasion of Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Ghazi (Gragn) in the 16th century.

saints.name: Presentation
saints.title: Feast of the Presentation of Our Lord (Timkat Mariam)
saints.notes: The Presentation of the Child Jesus in the Temple.

saints.name: Gebre Menfes Kidus
saints.title: Gebre Menfes Kidus
saints.notes: Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus (Ge'ez: አቡነ ገብረ መንፈስ ቅዱስ; also familiarly called Abo; born 29 December 829 E.C.) was an Egyptian Christian saint, and the founder of the monastery of Zuqualla. The fifth day of every month in the Ethiopian calendar is dedicated to this saint. Manuscripts differ in relating the story of the life of Gebre Menfes Kidus and the miracles he performed.

saints.name: St. Gebre Menfes Qiddus
saints.title: Saint Gebre Menfes Qiddus (Abbo), the Hermit Saint of Ethiopia
saints.notes: Known as Abbo, Gebre Menfes Qiddus (14th century) is one of the most beloved Ethiopian saints. He lived as an ascetic in the wilderness, sharing food with wild animals. He is depicted surrounded by lions and leopards.

saints.name: Abba Alef
saints.title: Abba Alef
saints.notes: Abba ‘Aléf was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. He is known for founding a monastery in Bi’isa (or Beheza) in Ahseya. His feast day is on 11 Mäggabit (20 March).

saints.name: St. Abba Betre Mariam
saints.title: Saint Abba Betre Mariam of Lake Tana
saints.notes: Abba Betre Mariam is a venerated Ethiopian monastic saint associated with the monasteries of Lake Tana.

saints.name: Annunciation
saints.title: Feast of the Annunciation (Lidata le-Mariam)
saints.notes: The Annunciation of the Archangel Gabriel to the Virgin Mary.

saints.name: Apostles Philip and James
saints.title: Feast of the Holy Apostles Philip and James the Less
saints.notes: Ethiopian commemoration of the Holy Apostles Philip and James (the Less).

saints.name: St. Abba Guba
saints.title: Saint Abba Guba, Desert Father of the Scetis (Ethiopia)
saints.notes: One of the Desert Fathers venerated in the Ethiopian church.

saints.name: Saint Abraham (Ethiopian)
saints.title: Saint Abraham (Ethiopian)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Lideta Maryam
saints.title: Lideta Maryam
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: St. Yared
saints.title: Saint Yared the Hymnographer, Father of Ethiopian Sacred Music
saints.notes: Saint Yared (505–571 AD) composed the three modes of Ethiopian liturgical chant: Ge'ez (joyful), Ezel (mourning), and Araray (ordinary time). Tradition says three birds from Paradise taught him the divine melodies. His work is still used unchanged today.

saints.name: Yared
saints.title: Yared
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: St. Mary
saints.title: Monthly Feast of St. Mary (Ginbot)
saints.notes: Monthly commemoration of the Blessed Virgin Mary (21st of Ginbot = June 1 Gregorian).

saints.name: Ablak (saint)
saints.title: Ablak (saint)
saints.notes: Ablak is a saint of the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church. His feast day is kept on 30 May.

saints.name: Abba Aftse
saints.title: Abba Aftse
saints.notes: Abba Aftse or ‘Afsé (probably fl. late 400s and early 500s A.D.) was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. As he has a Syriac name, he likely came from Edessa or its surroundings.

saints.name: Abba Guba
saints.title: Abba Guba
saints.notes: Abba Guba was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. He is known as a healer who founded a monastery in Madara, Ethiopia. Abba Guba probably originated from Cilicia.

saints.name: St. Samuel of Waldebba
saints.title: Saint Samuel of Waldebba, Founder of Waldebba Monastery
saints.notes: Samuel of Waldebba (14th century) founded the famous Waldebba Monastery in northern Ethiopia. Known for his strict ascetic life and miraculous healings.

saints.name: St. Lalibela
saints.title: Saint Lalibela, Righteous King and Builder of the Rock-Hewn Churches
saints.notes: King Lalibela (c. 1181–1221) commissioned eleven rock-hewn monolithic churches in Roha (now Lalibela), a UNESCO World Heritage Site. He intended the site as a New Jerusalem for Ethiopian Christians who could not travel to the Holy Land.

saints.name: Abba Garima
saints.title: Abba Garima
saints.notes: Abba Gärima (Geʽez: አባ ገሪማ; also known as Abba Yeshaq; fl. c. late 400s and early 500s A.D.), was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia.

saints.name: St. Abba Yohannes
saints.title: Saint Abba Yohannes of Debre Bizen Monastery
saints.notes: Abba Yohannes founded Debre Bizen monastery in Eritrea in the 14th century. It remains one of the most important monasteries of the Ethiopian Orthodox Church.

saints.name: Apostles Peter and Paul
saints.title: Feast of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul
saints.notes: Ethiopian commemoration of the Holy Apostles Peter and Paul, martyred in Rome.

saints.name: St. Abba Libanos
saints.title: Saint Abba Libanos, One of the Nine Saints
saints.notes: Abba Libanos is one of the Nine Saints who came from Rome to Ethiopia in the 5th century. He founded Debre Libanos in Tigray (distinct from Debre Libanos of Tekle Haymanot).

saints.name: Giyorgis of Segla
saints.title: Giyorgis of Segla
saints.notes: Giyorgis of Segla (c. 1365 – 1 July 1425), also known as Giyorgis of Gasicha or Abba Giyorgis, was an Ethiopian Oriental Orthodox monk, saint, and author of religious books. Giyorgis' work has had great influence on Ethiopian monastic calendars, hymns and Ge'ez literature.

saints.name: Apostle Thomas
saints.title: Feast of the Apostle Thomas
saints.notes: Ethiopian commemoration of St. Thomas the Apostle who brought Christianity to India.

saints.name: Transfiguration
saints.title: Feast of the Transfiguration (Buhe)
saints.notes: The Transfiguration of Our Lord, celebrated as Buhe in Ethiopia. Children sing songs and carry torches the eve before.

saints.name: The Nine Saints
saints.title: The Nine Saints (Tsatew Qiddusan), Missionaries to Ethiopia
saints.notes: The Nine Saints (5th century) were missionaries from Syria, Constantinople, and Rome who came to Ethiopia after the Council of Chalcedon. They founded monasteries and translated the Bible into Ge'ez.

saints.name: Seven Sleepers
saints.title: Holy Seven Sleepers of Ephesus
saints.notes: The Seven Sleepers (Seba Wedikat) are commemorated in the Ethiopian synaxarium. Seven young men who fled Decius's persecution and miraculously slept 300 years in a cave near Ephesus.

saints.name: St. Abba Libanos (Younger)
saints.title: Saint Abba Libanos the Younger of Debre Libanos
saints.notes: A later saint of Debre Libanos monastery, venerated for his holiness.

saints.name: 22 – Filseta
saints.title: 22 – Filseta
saints.notes: Filseta (Ge'ez: ፍልሰታ, romanized: Fəlsäta, lit. 'Movement', i.e. 'Assumption') is a feast day observed by the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Church (as well as the Ethiopian Catholic Church and the Eritrean Catholic Church) in commemoration of the Dormition and Assumption of Mary.

saints.name: St. Athanasius
saints.title: Saint Athanasius of Alexandria, Defender of Orthodoxy
saints.notes: St. Athanasius the Great (296–373), Archbishop of Alexandria, defended the Nicene Creed against Arianism. As Patriarch of Alexandria he consecrated Frumentius as the first Bishop of Ethiopia.

saints.name: Assumption
saints.title: Feast of the Assumption of the Blessed Virgin Mary
saints.notes: Ethiopian celebration of the Dormition and Assumption of the Virgin Mary.

saints.name: Moses the Black
saints.title: Moses the Black
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: St. Tekle Haymanot
saints.title: Saint Tekle Haymanot of Debre Libanos, Pillar of Ethiopian Monasticism
saints.notes: The greatest Ethiopian saint, Abba Tekle Haymanot (c. 1215–1313) founded Ethiopian monasticism at Debre Asbo (Debre Libanos). He is depicted with one leg and six wings, symbolizing that he stood in prayer for 22 years, one leg falling off after 7 years.

saints.name: Kristos Samra
saints.title: Kristos Samra
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Tekle Haymanot
saints.title: Tekle Haymanot
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Abnodius
saints.title: Abnodius
saints.notes: Abnodius is a saint of Ethiopia (Abyssinia). He is venerated in the Coptic Church on 3 September.

saints.name: St. John the Baptist
saints.title: Feast of John the Baptist (Ye-Yohannes Lidat)
saints.notes: Ethiopian celebration of the birth of St. John the Baptist in Pagume (the 13th short month).

saints.name: Lideta Mariam
saints.title: Lideta Mariam
saints.notes: The Nativity of the Blessed Virgin Mary, the Nativity of Mary, Marymas or the Birth of the Virgin Mary, refers to a Christian feast day celebrating the birth of Mary, mother of Jesus. The modern Biblical canon does not record Mary's birth. The earliest known account of Mary's birth is found in the Gospel of James (5:2),  an apocryphal text from the late second century, with her parents known as Sa

saints.name: Lideta (Birth of the Holy Virgin Mary) and Elias (Elijah)
saints.title: Lideta (Birth of the Holy Virgin Mary) and Elias (Elijah)
saints.notes: Elijah ( ih-LEYE-zhə or ih-LEYE-jə; Hebrew: אֵלִיָּהוּ, romanized: ʾĒlīyyāhu or אֵלִיָּה, ʾĒlīyyā, 'My God is Yahweh/YHWH') was a prophet and miracle worker who lived in the northern kingdom of Israel during the reign of King Ahab (9th century BC), according to the Books of Kings in the Hebrew Bible. In 1 Kings 18, Elijah defended the worship of the Hebrew deity Yahweh over that of the Canaanite d

saints.name: Enkutatash (Ethiopian New Year)
saints.title: Enkutatash — Ethiopian New Year (Meskerem 1)
saints.notes: Enkutatash is the Ethiopian New Year celebrated on Meskerem 1 (September 11 Gregorian). The name means "gift of jewels" — when King Solomon returned the Queen of Sheba to Ethiopia, he gave her jewels. Children give flowers and sing songs, while new paintings are shared. The Ethiopian Orthodox Church celebrates Lideta le-Maryam (Birth of the Virgin Mary) on the same day.

saints.name: Kidus Thaddeus
saints.title: Kidus Thaddeus
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 2th of every Geʼez month

saints.name: Thaddius
saints.title: Thaddius
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Ba'eta Mariam
saints.title: Ba'eta Mariam
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 3th of every Geʼez month

saints.name: Be'eta (Presentation of the Holy Virgin to the Temple of Jerusalem)
saints.title: Be'eta (Presentation of the Holy Virgin to the Temple of Jerusalem)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Yohannis Wolde Negedguad
saints.title: Yohannis Wolde Negedguad
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 4th of every Geʼez month

saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Abune Gebre Menfes Kidus and Petros we Paulos
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 5th of every Geʼez month

saints.title: Petros and Paulos (Peter and Paul) and Gebre Menfes Kiddus
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Kidist Arsema
saints.title: Kidist Arsema
saints.notes: Hripsime (Armenian: Հռիփսիմէ; died c. 290) was a martyr of Roman origin. The story of her martyrdom is connected with the traditional account of the Christianization of Armenia.

saints.name: Our Lady of Qusquam (Egypt)
saints.title: Our Lady of Qusquam (Egypt)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.notes: The Trinity (Latin: Trinitas, lit. 'triad', from trinus 'threefold') is a Christian doctrine concerning the nature of God, which defines one God existing in three coeternal, consubstantial divine persons: God the Father, God the Son (Jesus Christ), and God the Holy Spirit, three distinct persons (hypostases) sharing one essence/substance/nature (homoousion). saints.name: Holy Trinity Day
saints.title: Holy Trinity Day
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Kidus Kiros and Abba Banuda
saints.notes: Cyrus of Alexandria (Arabic: المقوقس al-Muqawqis, Greek: Κῦρος Ἀλεξανδρείας; d. 21 March 642) was a prominent figure in the 7th century. He served as a Greek Orthodox Patriarch of Alexandria and held the position of the second-last Byzantine prefect of Egypt.

saints.name: Kiros (Cyrus) and Abba Banuda
saints.title: Kiros (Cyrus) and Abba Banuda
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Kidus Thomas
saints.notes: Thomas the Apostle (Classical Syriac: ܬܐܘܡܐ, romanized: Tʾōmā, lit. 'the Twin') also known as Didymus (Greek: Δίδυμος, romanized: Dídymos 'twin'), was one of the Twelve Apostles of Jesus according to the New Testament. saints.title: Thomas (not the Apostle)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Kidus Meskel
saints.notes: In Christian tradition, the True Cross is the original wooden cross on which Jesus of Nazareth was crucified. It is related by numerous historical accounts and legends that Helen, the mother of Roman emperor Constantine the Great, recovered the True Cross at the Holy Sepulchre in Jerusalem, when she travelled to the Holy Land in the years 326–328. saints.title: Kidus Meskel (Feast of the Holy Cross)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Hannah we Iyachem (Kidist Dingle Mariams parents)
saints.notes: Mary was a first-century Jewish woman of Nazareth, the wife of Joseph and the mother of Jesus. She is an important figure of Christianity, venerated under various titles such as virgin or queen, many of which are mentioned in the Litany of Loreto. saints.title: Kidus Michael

In later Jewish tradition, he became identified as one of the three heavenly visitors entertained by Abraham at the Oak of Mamre. saints.title: Feast of Igziabher Ab (God the Father) and Raphael the Archangel
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.title: Abune Aregawi and Gebre Chistos
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 14th of every Geʼez month

saints.name: Abuna Aregawi and Gebre Kristos
saints.title: Abuna Aregawi and Gebre Kristos
saints.notes: Abuna Aregawi (also called Za-Mika'el Aragawi) was a sixth-century Syrian monk and canonized by the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, as well as by the Ethiopian Catholic Church, as well as the Eritrean Orthodox Church. saints.name: Kidus Kirkos and Iyalota
saints.title: Kidus Kirkos and Iyalota
saints.notes: Cyricus and his mother Julitta are venerated as early Christian martyrs. According to traditional stories, they were put to death at Tarsus in AD 304.

saints.name: Kirkos and his mother Iyeluta (Cyricus and Julitta)
saints.title: Kirkos and his mother Iyeluta (Cyricus and Julitta)
saints.notes: Cyricus and his mother Julitta are venerated as early Christian martyrs. According to traditional stories, they were put to death at Tarsus in AD 304.

saints.title: Kidist Kidanemihret
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church — commemorated on the 16th of every Geʼez month

saints.title: Kidane Mihret (Our Lady Covenant of Mercy)
saints.notes: Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church

saints.name: Meskel
saints.title: Finding of the True Cross (Meskel)
saints.notes: Meskel celebrates the finding of the True Cross by Empress Helena. Enormous bonfires (Demera) are lit throughout Ethiopia the eve of Meskel.

saints.title: Kidus Estifanos and Abba Gerima

He was a forceful advocate for the observation of the Sabbath in Christianity. His followers, known as the House of Ewost

saints.name: Absadi
saints.title: Absadi
saints.notes: Abba Absadi (died 1381) is a saint of the Ethiopian and Eritrean Orthodox Tewahedo Churches. He was a disciple of Ewostatewos, and his best-known disciple is Abba Filipos. He founded the monastery of Debre Mariam in 1374, which is located in modern-day Eritrea.

saints.name: Kidus Gebriel
saints.title: Kidus Gebriel
saints.notes: In Judaism, Christianity, Islam, and other Abrahamic religions, Gabriel ( GAY-bree-əl) or Cebrail (Djebraïl) in some cultures, is an archangel with the power to announce God's will to humankind as the messenger of God. He is mentioned in the Hebrew Bible, the New Testament and the Quran. In the Book of Daniel, Gabriel appears to the prophet Daniel to explain his visions.

saints.title: Gabriel the Archangel

saints.title: Kidus Giorgis
saints.notes: Saint George (Greek: Γεώργιος, romanized: Geṓrgioscode: ell promoted to code: el ; died 23 April 303), also George of Lydda, was an early Christian martyr who is venerated as a saint in Christianity. According to holy tradition, he was a soldier in the Roman army. Of Cappadocian Greek origin, he became a member of the Praetorian Guard for Roman emperor Diocletian.

saints.name: Abune Teklehaimanot & Christos Samra
saints.title: Abune Teklehaimanot & Christos Samra
saints.notes: Tekle Haymanot (Ge'ez: አቡነ ተክለ ሃይማኖት; known in the Coptic Church as Saint Takla Haymanot of Ethiopia; 1215–1313) was an Ethiopian saint and monk mostly venerated as a hermit. He was the Abuna of Ethiopia who founded a major monastery in his native province of Shewa. He is significant for being the only Ethiopian saint popular both amongst Ethiopians and outside that country.

He was born in the city of Eskentos in Cappadocia, in Eastern Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey). According to Christian tradition, he was the soldier who killed Julian the Apostate during his campaign

saints.name: St. Ewostatewos
saints.title: Saint Ewostatewos (Eustathius) of Ethiopia, Monastic Reformer
saints.notes: Ewostatewos (c. 1273–1352) was an Ethiopian monk who insisted on Sabbath observance and reformed Ethiopian monasticism. He spent his last years in exile in Egypt and Armenia. The Ewostathian monastic movement shaped Ethiopian Christianity.

saints.name: St. Abba Gerima
saints.title: Saint Abba Gerima (Isaac), One of the Nine Saints
saints.notes: Abba Gerima (Isaac) was one of the Nine Saints from Rome. He founded Debre Gerima monastery in Tigray, one of the oldest monasteries in Ethiopia.

saints.name: St. Dioscorus
saints.title: Saint Dioscorus of Alexandria, Fifth Pope of Alexandria
saints.notes: Dioscorus I was the fifth Pope of Alexandria (444–451) who upheld Cyril's theology at the Council of Chalcedon but was deposed and exiled by the Chalcedonian majority. Venerated as a saint by the Oriental Orthodox churches.

saints.name: Abuna Aregawi
saints.title: Abuna Aregawi
saints.notes: Abuna Aregawi (also called Za-Mika'el Aragawi) was a sixth-century Syrian monk and canonized by the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church, as well as by the Ethiopian Catholic Church, as well as the Eritrean Orthodox Church. saints.name: Abba Yem'ata
saints.title: Abba Yem'ata
saints.notes: Abba Yäm’ata or Yem’ata (probably fl. late 400s and early 500s A.D.) was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. He founded a monastery in Gär’alta in Endärta woreda, Tigray Region.

saints.name: Emperor Zara Yaqob
saints.title: Saint Zara Yaqob (Emperor Zara Yaqob), Defender of the Faith
saints.notes: Emperor Zara Yaqob (r. 1434–1468) defended Ethiopian Christianity, commissioned theological writings, and standardized the Ethiopian church calendar. He enforced strict observance of Marian feasts and church reforms.

saints.name: Kidana Mehret
saints.title: Feast of the Holy Covenant (Kidana Mehret) of Our Lady
saints.notes: The Covenant of Mercy — Our Lady's promise to intercede for Ethiopia. One of the most celebrated Marian feasts in the Ethiopian church.

saints.title: Abba Liqanos
saints.notes: Abba Liqanos (probably fl. late 400s and early 500s A.D.) was one of the Nine Saints of Ethiopia. He is known as a composer of hymns and liturgies.

saints.name: Martyrs of Nagran
saints.title: The Holy Martyrs of Nagran (Arabia Felix)
saints.notes: Christians of Nagran (Yemen) martyred by the Jewish-Yemenite king Dhu Nuwas in 523 AD for refusing to apostatize. Ethiopia's Emperor Kaleb later invaded Yemen to avenge them. Commemorated in the Ethiopian synaxarium.

saints.name: Frumentius
saints.title: Frumentius
saints.notes: Frumentius (Ge'ez: ፍሬምናጦስ, Latin: Sanctus Frumentius; died c. 383) was a Phoenician Christian missionary and the first bishop of Axum who brought Christianity to the Kingdom of Aksum. He is sometimes known by other names, such as Abuna ("Our Father") and Aba Selama ("Father of Peace").
